Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella tells industry: Software is not going anywhere but ...
Article Text:
Satya Nadella

So much of what we do at work is still spent working around software. We switch between apps, rebuild context each time, and translate what we want to do into the steps each system expects. AI is changing that, helping us organize software around the work, rather than us working around the software.

We’ve already seen an early version of this shift in software development, one of the first areas to adopt agents at scale.

As agentic development has grown, GitHub has seen accelerating repo creation and PR and commit activity. The lesson is that more agents don’t make systems of record less important. They make trusted places to maintain information, coordinate changes, and manage state even more important. We see a similar pattern in sales, customer service, finance, and ops.

It’s why our ambition is to make Copilot a new OS for work that spans every model, every form factor, and every task.

Merging the ‘head’ with the ‘headless’ layer

But a new front end like Copilot (the “head”) is only half the story. We also need a governed foundation that makes the underlying business logic and context historically locked inside individual CRM, ERP, and other apps available to agents (the “headless” layer).

After all, a model’s intelligence only becomes useful to a business when it has the right context and the right tools to act. You need a system that can understand someone’s intent, bring in the relevant organizational and business context, and invoke the right workflows.

For us, that means bringing together Copilot as the multi-model harness and agentic layer, the business logic in our apps, and the systems of record they run on, combined with connectors to other data sources.

Microsoft IQ connects those layers together.

This gives Copilot and agents a rich understanding of the business, connecting organizational knowledge with business data, processes and tools so they can reason over the work and act within the rules of the enterprise. It is not just about exposing existing APIs to an LLM, but architecting business context itself for AI.

It’s why today we announced 30+ new Copilot skills across Dynamics 365 Sales, Service and Customer Insights, as Jeff explains here, bringing these CRM capabilities directly into the flow of work.

And it’s just the start for us.

With these skills, you can use Copilot across Chat, Cowork, Autopilot, and even Code to complete even more end to end workflows across your business.

But it’s not just about getting work done with Copilot.

We’ve also introduced

Microsoft Copilot

Managed Runtime, which provides hosting infra which lets code run safely inside your company’s environment, governed by IT.

When you put it all together, you get something much more powerful than yet another AI feature inside SaaS. You start to get what I think of as an infinite SaaS factory.

Think about simply going to Code in Copilot, describing what your business needs, and building a customization or an entirely new Saas module.

With these plugins and skills, you can extend our Dataverse schema, build on existing business logic, and create new experiences and workflows connected to the systems your business already runs on.

We are entering a new era of truly “personal” software, where you can easily tailor the apps you use to the way you work, but stay connected to the systems of record your business already runs on, preventing fragmentation of your most important systems.

And the opportunity is bigger than simply extending the systems we have today. We can reinvent systems of record for an agentic world to handle high-volume agent access, bring together context and intelligence across data sources, and work natively with assistants like Copilot. For some customers, that will mean extending existing systems. For others, it will mean replacing them.

With Code and these underlying skills, you are doing all this with essentially zero friction, meaning it’s easy to quickly customize what you build and adapt from one project to another as your business changes.

And importantly this is not about using an LLM for everything. Because these skills are deeply integrated with your systems of record, we can use tokens where intelligence actually adds value, while relying on deterministic software for execution when that is faster, cheaper and more reliable.

I believe all this can reset business SaaS.

The opportunity is to reinvent systems of record for an agentic world, not just build new experiences on top of them, while giving every business an entirely new way to orchestrate work and build what is missing.

That is the direction we are taking at Microsoft: Copilot as a new OS for work, with a governed infinite SaaS factory built in.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has suggested that software is not going anywhere and once again, argued autonomous agents and generative tools are fundamentally reorganising how people interact with corporate technology, essentially helping people organise software around the work, rather than them working around the software. Speaking on the changing architecture of enterprise tools, Nadella explained in a post on X (formerly Twitter) that workers have spent decades having to “work around software”, wasting hours toggling between siloed applications, rebuilding lost context and translating tasks into rigid database commands.According to Nadella, artificial intelligence reverses that dynamic, organising software around actual tasks rather than forcing humans to adapt to fragmented tools. Nadella pointed to early trends in software engineering on GitHub as proof that agentic tools do not diminish traditional platforms. Despite autonomous coding agents completing large volumes of work, GitHub has experienced accelerating repository creation, along with higher pull-request and commit activity.Microsoft’s overarching ambition is to turn Copilot into a universal operating system for work that spans every underlying model, computing form factor, and daily assignment.Nadella emphasised that deploying an intuitive user interface – the “head” – is only half the equation. Enterprise agents require governed access to the “headless” layer where business logic and operational records reside inside CRM and ERP suites. Here’s how he explained this:
Article Summary: Microsoft has announced 30+ new Copilot skills across Dynamics 365 Sales, Service and Customer Insights. The skills are deeply integrated with your systems of record. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella believes this is the direction we are taking at Microsoft.

Article Title: Is the Apple iPhone 17 worth buying in this year’s festive season sales
Article Text:
The festive iPhone to buy

The festive discount on the iPhone 17 mostly undoes Apple’s price hike

A year on, the iPhone 17 has aged better than most base iPhones

The iPhone 17 still makes more sense than waiting or going older

Every festive sale, the iPhone that actually moves is last year's. The new model gets the spotlight and the billboards, while the outgoing one, suddenly a lot cheaper, quietly ends up in most shopping carts. It went that way with the iPhone 13 in 2022, the iPhone 14 a year later and the 15 and 16 after that, so it's no surprise to see the iPhone 17 headlining this week's festive sales.What's different this year is that the iPhone 17 has nothing to make way for. Apple unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and the foldable iPhone Duo in September but held back the regular iPhone 18, which isn't expected before early 2027. For once, last year's iPhone is also the newest regular one on the shelf, and that makes it the festive pick more than it has ever been.The only catch is the price tag. The iPhone 17 went on sale in India in September 2025 at Rs 82,900 for 256GB, and once the iPhone 18 Pro arrived, Apple moved it up to Rs 99,900. The phone now costs Rs 17,000 more than it did on day one, so it pays to look closely at what this year's festive offers actually save.Take Flipkart's offer, the one most buyers will have come across this week. The 256GB iPhone 17 sells for Rs 84,999 during Big Billion Days, an ICICI Bank or Axis Bank credit card takes off another Rs 2,000, and trading in an old phone adds an exchange bonus of up to Rs 3,000 on top of its value.Stack all three and you arrive at the Rs 79,999 figure doing the rounds.Flipkart is only one of many, though, with iPhone 17 offers running across online platforms and retail stores this festive season, and a few examples show how varied they are. Reliance Digital has the phone at Rs 79,899 and bank and exchange offers that can bring it to around Rs 69,000. Retailer Unicorn, meanwhile, isn't waiting for a sale at all, putting the iPhone 17 at an effective Rs 78,900 in its stores once up to Rs 5,000 in instant cashback on Axis Bank, ICICI Bank and SBI Card credit cards and an exchange bonus of up to Rs 8,000 are counted, with no-cost EMI stretching to 24 months.Without the right credit card or an old phone to trade in, you're paying roughly what buyers paid last September. Most of the festive discount, in other words, is the hike being walked back.And the search doesn't have to stay online. Other retailers, and even the neighbourhood electronics store, often match these prices through the festive season, so they're worth a visit too.Wherever you end up buying it, paying close to last year's price still counts for plenty this year, with new phones arriving well above the ones they replace. The iPhone 18 Pro, for one, starts at Rs 1,64,900, a full Rs 30,000 more than the iPhone 17 Pro did, so for a current-generation iPhone, that is about as generous as things are likely to get for a while.It helps that the phone itself has worn its first year well. The iPhone 17 was the first regular iPhone in a long while to leave very little on the table for the Pro models, bringing a 120Hz ProMotion display with always-on after years of the base iPhone sitting at 60Hz while Android phones at half the price moved on. Storage doubled to 256GB, the ultrawide jumped from 12 to 48 megapixels, and an 18-megapixel square selfie sensor let Center Stage widen the frame as friends crowded in, without anyone turning the phone sideways.None of that feels dated a year later. The iPhone 17 has been my everyday phone through that entire stretch. The A19 hasn't lost its edge either, and still handles editing photos, bouncing between work chats and a dozen browser tabs, or even a long evening of gaming without a hiccup without a stutter, and everything on that 120Hz screen still feels as snappy as it did on day one.The battery, rated at up to 30 hours of video playback, still gets me comfortably through to bedtime with the always-on display switched on. The cameras have aged just as well, with the 48-megapixel pair still turning out sharp, natural-looking photos by day and dependable ones at night.The software has moved along as well. iOS 26 arrived with its share of grumbles, from a Liquid Glass design that made parts of the interface harder to read to Apple Intelligence feeling thin without the Siri overhaul people had been waiting for. iOS 27 has put much of its effort into smoothing those rough edges, and it finally brings that Siri along.That new Siri AI is the biggest change the iPhone 17 has seen since it went on sale. Siri can now hold a proper conversation, answer open-ended questions, read what's on screen and draw on messages and documents on the phone, while a new Camera mode can split a bill from a photo of the receipt. It works in English in India for now, with Hindi still to come.What it lacked last year, of course, it still lacks. There's no telephoto camera, so zooming past 2x means cropping. At 6.3 inches it is nowhere near the compact iPhones a loyal few still miss. If either was a dealbreaker in 2025, a discounted price tag won't change that now.If you’re still on the fence, it’s worth going back to what I made of the iPhone 17 when I first used it last year . Just keep the changes covered here in mind as you read it.Holding out usually pays off only when the next model promises a lot more for the same money, and this time the signs point to neither. The iPhone 18 is expected around March alongside the iPhone 18e, and the bigger changes, including a smaller Dynamic Island and new cameras, look set to stay with the Pro models. With prices where they're headed, expecting it to land at Rs 99,900, let alone below it, is wishful thinking too.Which is why the old festive rule of picking last year's iPhone has rarely been easier to follow. Anyone still on an iPhone 13, iPhone 14 or older, especially a 60Hz model whose battery has seen better days, will feel the jump the first time they scroll, and so will Android users who have wanted an iPhone without paying Pro prices. iPhone 16 owners are the ones who can sit this one out, since a smoother screen alone is a hard sell for another Rs 80,000.The iPhone 16 is also the obvious alternative on sale, going for somewhere between Rs 65,000 and Rs 72,000. It costs less today, but it does without the 120Hz screen and the upgraded cameras, which happen to be what will keep the 17 feeling current four or five years down the line. Step further back to the iPhone 15, which Flipkart has from Rs 63,999, and Siri AI goes off the table altogether.So yes, this year's festive discount is mostly a price correction. But last year's iPhone has been the smart festive buy for a while now, and with no new regular model sitting beside it, the iPhone 17 has never had an easier case to make. If you need an iPhone before March, this is the one to get.
Article Summary: The festive discount on the iPhone 17 mostly undoes Apple’s price hike. The iPhone 17 went on sale in India in September 2025 at Rs 82,900 for 256GB. Once the iPhone 18 Pro arrived, Apple moved it up to Rs 99,900. The phone now costs Rs 17,000 more than it did on day one.

Article Title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff warning on AI has a 'cautionary tale'; goes back to days he called Facebook 'new cigarette'; says that a lot of individuals got hurt
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

Avoiding making past mistakes, says Benioff

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff recently stepped into the mounting global debate around artificial intelligence (AI) safety, calling on technology leaders to exercise ethical responsibility as high-capability models spread rapidly across global markets. His remarks arrive amid intensifying friction across Silicon Valley, spurred largely by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s 3,800-word essay demanding an industrywide slowdown in frontier model deployment to let technical safeguards catch up.According to a report by CNBC, Benioff has an established track record of pushing tech giants toward social responsibility. For years, he served as a prominent critic of big tech and social media networks, making headlines in 2018 when he declared that “Facebook is the new cigarettes” while demanding aggressive federal oversight.Speaking at Salesforce’s annual Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, Benioff drew a direct parallel between the early missteps of social networking platforms and the current generative AI wave. He said: “A lot of companies got hurt, a lot of individuals got hurt through social media. We don’t want that to happen in AI.”Despite the parallel, the Salesforce founder did not directly attack AI startups or endorse Amodei’s proposal to halt model development.Instead, he argued that developers must proactively evaluate the societal ripple effects of their software as innovation moves forward.“We want AI to take care of these things and be held responsible, and take care of these actions and be ethical. The heart of ethics is responsibility,” Benioff stated, calling on developers to treat safety as an obligation.“We really look at a light on our brethren here in San Francisco and all over the world and say, ‘We want you to be ethical in your actions and how you take care of your communities and the world,’ because this technology is very powerful.”Meanwhile, Salesforce collaborated with Anthropic, and Amodei joined Benioff on stage during the opening keynote on Tuesday, stating:“I think that’s the way to lead the industry forward, to set an example, to say that everyone can always be better.”
Article Summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff called on tech leaders to exercise ethical responsibility as high-capability models spread rapidly across global markets. His remarks arrive amid intensifying friction across Silicon Valley, spurred largely by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s 3,800-word essay.

Article Title: In 1982, Steve Jobs launched Apple's 'Kids Can't Wait' school giveaway; the programme put more than 9,000 computers into California classrooms, with software and free teacher training to help schools
Article Text:
In 1982, Steve Jobs launched Apple's 'Kids Can't Wait' school giveaway; the programme put more than 9,000 computers into California classrooms, with software and free teacher training to help schools use them

Why did Apple want computers in schools

Apple was not the only company targeting schools

In the early 1980s, personal computers were beginning to enter American schools, but many classrooms still had only a handful of machines. Apple wanted to change that. In 1982, the company launched a programme called “Kids Can't Wait”, with a plan to put a computer in every elementary and secondary school in the US. The nationwide plan depended on Congress approving tax benefits to help fund the donations. While the legislation faced delays, California lawmakers approved the tax benefit Apple had sought. The iPhone-maker then donated nearly 9,000 Apple IIe computers, along with software, to California schools. Per reports, the equipment was valued at $21 million.Apple was then competing with companies including IBM, Tandy, Atari and Commodore for a growing education market. In the early 1980s, the average American elementary school had reportedly 3.6 computers, while the average high school had 10.Computer makers then expected these numbers to rise quickly. Getting their machines into schools could help students learn computing on a particular brand and later encourage their families to buy the same products.“School use turns out to be absolutely key to establishing brand loyalty,” Clive Smith, an analyst at the Yankee Group, told TIME.At the time, Apple had already been offering steep discounts to universities. Its new Macintosh computer, which sold for $2,495, was offered to selected colleges for resale to students at just over $1,000. Two dozen universities, including Harvard, Yale and Stanford, accepted the offer and ordered more than 50,000 computers.Notably, other technology companies were also trying to win over schools through donations, discounts and training programmes. Tandy, which sold Radio Shack computers, provided educational materials and offered free instruction to teachers. Hewlett-Packard offered to donate 10 computers to each of 14 California high school districts, while Digital Equipment announced a donation of $1.1 million worth of equipment to 46 schools in New England.IBM was also working to expand its presence in education. It introduced teacher-training initiatives, gave 1,500 personal computers to teachers in 88 schools and announced plans to donate another 2,000 machines.At the time, Apple held nearly 50% of the primary and secondary school computer market, compared with 3.9% for IBM, according to the report.
Article Summary: Apple donated nearly 9,000 Apple IIe computers, along with software, to California schools. The equipment was valued at $21 million. Apple was competing with companies including IBM, Tandy, Atari and Commodore for the education market. Getting their machines into schools could help students learn computing on a particular brand.

Article Title: Jensen Huang and his wife Lori pledged $30 million to Stanford; in 2010, the university opened an engineering centre housing more than 270 faculty, staff and students, with workshops for building prot
Article Text:
What is the Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center

How the centre supports engineering research and innovation

"will foster future innovation and groundbreaking research for years to come."

Why Jensen Huang supported the engineering centre

"To build a better future we must invest in tomorrow's innovators,"

"There is no better place to do this than Stanford. Magic happens time and again when bright students learn together in an environment rich with faculty who are the best in their fields. With this new engineering center, we are giving students and teachers a place to collaborate and create our future. I hope that students will find inspiration here, and that Stanford will be as important in shaping their lives as it has been in mine.

"

The Huang Center's place in Stanford's campus

Jensen Huang and Lori helped fund Stanford’s engineering centre with their $30 million donation. The university dedicated the Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center as a shared space for research, education and collaboration across disciplines. The building houses more than 270 faculty members, staff and students, along with workshops for building prototypes and models.The centre was established as part of Stanford’s Science and Engineering Quad, providing a shared space for students and researchers working across engineering, science and medicine. Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia, received his master’s degree in electrical engineering from Stanford in 1992.The Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center was dedicated on October 5, 2010, as a new home for Stanford’s School of Engineering. The building was designed to serve as an academic and social destination for students and faculty, bringing together researchers from different departments and disciplines.The centre houses members of the Department of Management Science and Engineering, the Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering and the Stanford Technology Ventures Program.It also accommodates the School of Engineering’s Dean’s Office and supporting departments.The building features the 300-seat NVIDIA Auditorium and the Frederick Emmons Terman Engineering Library. The library was designed to support collaboration and help students and faculty access both digital and print research materials.The Huang Center was designed to encourage interaction between engineering researchers and colleagues in biology, chemistry, physics and medicine. Its open spaces, student lounges, and flexible furniture provide space for discussion and collaboration.​The building also includes workshops for constructing prototypes and models, allowing students to develop and test ideas. These facilities reflect the university’s approach to engineering education, which combines specialised technical knowledge with teamwork, communication, entrepreneurship and design.At the centre’s dedication, Stanford President John Hennessy said the buildingHennessy also thanked the Huangs for their support, saying their contribution reflected a tradition of alumni helping future generations access educational opportunities.Huang said the project was intended to give students and teachers a place to work together and develop new ideas.​Huang said.The centre was also designed to address changes in engineering education. James D. Plummer, then dean of Stanford’s School of Engineering, said engineers needed to develop expertise in their fields while learning to work across disciplines and navigate a global economy.Located in the Science and Engineering Quad, the building forms part of Stanford’s broader campus plan, connecting the university’s historic Main Quad with newer science and engineering facilities.Its design combines a modern interpretation of Stanford architecture with sustainability measures. The university said the Science and Engineering Quad buildings were designed to reduce potable water consumption by up to 90% and energy use by about 50% compared with buildings of similar size and use.Exhibits inside the centre highlight Stanford Engineering’s history of innovation and technology transfer. These include displays inspired by the garage where Hewlett-Packard began and servers used by Stanford graduate students Sergey Brin and Larry Page while developing the PageRank algorithm that led to Google.
Article Summary: The Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center was dedicated on October 5, 2010, as a new home for Stanford’s School of Engineering. The building houses more than 270 faculty members, staff and students, along with workshops for building prototypes and models. The Huang Center was designed to encourage interaction between engineering researchers and colleagues.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Andrew Carnegie: If you want to be happy, set a goal that commands your thoughts, liberates your energy, and inspires your hopes
Article Text:
Andrew Carnegie

What does Andrew Carnegie's quote mean

Other famous quotes by Andrew Carnegie

A library outranks any other one thing a community can do to benefit its people. It is a never failing spring in the desert.

As I grow older, I pay less attention to what men say. I just watch what they do.”

People who are unable to motivate themselves must be content with mediocrity, no matter how impressive their other talents.

If you want to be happy, set a goal that commands your thoughts, liberates your energy, and inspires your hopes.

A man who acquires the ability to take full possession of his own mind may take possession of anything else to which he is justly entitled.

No man becomes rich unless he enriches others.

Teamwork is the ability to work together toward a common vision. The ability to direct individual accomplishments toward organizational objectives. It is the fuel that allows common people to attain uncommon results.

Happiness is often linked to success, money or personal achievements. But Scottish-American industrialist and philanthropist Andrew Carnegie's words offer a different perspective. He believed that having a meaningful goal can give people a sense of direction, focus their efforts and keep their hopes alive. The Scottish-born American industrialist who became one of the world's wealthiest businessmen through the steel industry. After selling his steel company in 1901, he devoted much of his later life to philanthropy. Andrew Carnegie’s quote, “If you want to be happy, set a goal that commands your thoughts, liberates your energy, and inspires your hopes,” highlights the role that purpose can play in everyday life.The quote suggests that happiness can come from working towards something that matters to you. A clear goal gives the mind something meaningful to focus on, encourages people to put their abilities to use and gives them a reason to look forward to the future.The phrase “commands your thoughts” points to the importance of focus. When people have a clear aim, they may find it easier to organise their time and efforts instead of feeling lost or distracted.“Liberates your energy” suggests that a meaningful goal can encourage people to take action. Whether it is learning a new skill, building a business, improving one's health or helping others, having a purpose can make it easier to stay committed.The final phrase, “inspires your hopes,” highlights the importance of looking ahead. A goal gives people something to work towards, even when progress is slow or challenges arise.
Article Summary: Andrew Carnegie's famous quote: 'If you want to be happy, set a goal that commands your thoughts, liberates your energy' The Scottish-American industrialist believed that having a meaningful goal can give people a sense of direction and keep their hopes alive.

Article Title: As Americans vandalise Flock surveillance cameras across US, company has asked employees: Tell us if you want to ...
Article Text:
Flock is under pressure from regulators

Investor backing

Flock Safety, the US startup behind thousands of AI-powered surveillance cameras and licence plate readers deployed across the country, plans to lay off about 18% of its workforce following a voluntary buyout programme, according to a Reuters report. The move comes as the company faces mounting scrutiny from privacy advocates, lawmakers and communities increasingly pushing back against its technology.People familiar with the matter told Reuters that the job cuts are expected to affect roughly 270 employees. The departures will take effect at the end of the month. The layoffs follow a voluntary separation programme launched by the company in September, which encouraged employees to apply if they wished to leave. Flock currently employs about 1,500 people. Flock Safety declined to comment on the plans. Reuters reported that the Atlanta-based company has not yet publicly announced the layoffs.In September, Flock announced a voluntary separation program asking employees to apply if they wanted to leave, Wired reported last month. The Atlanta-based company has about 1,500 employees.Flock is under pressure from regulators, lawmakers and privacy advocates, even as it continues to draw strong interest from venture capital investors.A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found Americans divided: 38% support using Flock cameras in their community, while 47% oppose it.The company's network of around 120,000 AI-powered cameras, mounted on streets and highways across 49 states, automatically reads license plates and records passing vehicles. Flock provides cameras and software to more than 4,800 law enforcement agencies and nearly 1,000 businesses. It says its technology helps investigators solve crimes, but it has faced growing criticism over alleged privacy violations and data-sharing practices.The backlash has produced concrete consequences:* Florida: In September, the state banned automated license plate readers from state highways, citing privacy risks tied to Flock's cameras.* Home Depot: Investors recently demanded reviews of the retailer's partnerships with surveillance technology vendors, after reports that Flock's data was used in immigration enforcement.* Virginia: Flock faces a privacy lawsuit alleging that the widespread deployment of its AI-powered cameras amounts to warrantless surveillance.* Midterms: Together with AI data centers, Flock cameras have become a flashpoint in this year's elections, with candidates increasingly attacking opponents by linking them to the technology.Founded in 2017, Flock has raised more than $950 million from venture capital investors. Its latest round, $275 million in March led by Andreessen Horowitz, valued the company at $7.5 billion. The company has said the funds support a new US manufacturing facility and an upcoming push into drone products.
Article Summary: Flock Safety, the US startup behind thousands of AI-powered surveillance cameras and licence plate readers, plans to lay off about 18% of its workforce. Article Title: OpenAI tells the world why it fired three of its top researchers; writes open letter saying, ‘Our internal investigation uncovered…’
Article Text:
What note from OpenAI research leaders said

A note from our research leaders:

Last week we parted ways with Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek after a thorough investigation found they violated clear policies on handling sensitive information.

Our internal investigation uncovered a significant breach of trust beyond what’s outlined in the letter they published and we stand by the decision to not continue their employment. We generally keep individual employment matters private and don't believe a back and forth would be productive or lead to a resolution, but we want to address the points they raised in their letter directly.

- We want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out.

Safety and research debates happen every day at OpenAI, often spirited and highly critical. We actively encourage these discussions and consider them essential to making the right decisions. We cannot do the work in front of us without a high degree of trust. We will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes.

We have not and do not terminate any of our employees for raising concerns.

- We are actively finalizing contracts with third-party safety assessors and will announce details in the coming weeks.

People across the company have been working really hard on getting these partnerships up and running. We are committed to embedding external assessors and continue to make close collaboration with independent safety organizations a core part of our safety work. Many of our researchers already work with 3p safety organizations productively.

- We agree with the letter that preserving the monitorability of frontier models requires an industry-wide commitment, including from OpenAI.

Monitorability has long been a core piece of our research program, and something we continue to invest significant resources in (see our publications on Monitoring Monitorability and the subsequent open sourcing of monitorability evals, our system card for GPT-6 Astra, Jakub’s blog and post on X, and the numerous blog posts on our Alignment blog on the topic).

We are deeply sad about this outcome. We appreciated Jasmine, Mikita, and Tomek’s contributions to AI safety at OpenAI and their willingness to speak up and challenge ideas.

We championed their voices, supported their work, and placed enormous trust in them. These decisions were not about them raising safety concerns. We have always encouraged that and always will.

Fired engineers publish letter to OpenAI board
Article Summary: A note from OpenAI's research leaders addresses the firing of three engineers. The engineers violated policies on handling sensitive information, the note says. The company says it is committed to embedding external safety assessors in its research program. The team will continue to be extremely forgiving of our team making good-faith mistakes, it says.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos and Leonardo DiCaprio launched $200 million project to save 100 of Earth's most threatened species, from lemurs, salamanders to pangolins
Article Text:
PC: Forbes

The project stems from an idea that DiCaprio

Species in the protected project

Long-term conservation support

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and actor-environmentalist Leonardo DiCaprio have launched a $200 million conservation initiative which is aimed at helping 100 of the world’s most threatened species recover from the brink of extinction. As reported by Fortune, the foundation backed by Bezos and DiCaprio have infield the Phoenix Species Project, which they describe as the largest single fund dedicated exclusively to recovering critically endangered species. The initiative is being led by Re:wild, the conservation organisation co-founded by Dicaprio, and the Bezos Earth Fund, chaired by Bezos. The program is said to offer funding, technical expertise and long-term support to conservation groups working to protect facing severe threats from habitat loss, climate change and other environmental pressures.The project came into life with the idea that DiCaprio had been developing for years around creating a large-scale coordinated effort to rescue species whose survival is increasingly threatened by climate change. In the year 2021, DiCaprio and Wes Secret, chief executive and co-founder of Re:wild, met with Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez Bezos, who serve as chair and vice chair respectively of the Bezos Earth Fund.The discussions were followed by consultations with governments, environmental organisations and Indigenous communities, eventually leading to the creation of the Phoenix Species Project.The initiative's targets include:* Golden-crowned sifaka: a lemur from Madagascar.* Hickory Nut Gorge green salamander: a lungless tree-dweller found only in a small canyon in North Carolina.* Visayan warty pig: native to islands in the Philippines.* Cozumel harvest mouse: found only on an island off Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula.* Pink land iguana: found only on Wolf Volcano in the Galápagos Islands.* Malayan (Sunda) pangolin: native to Southeast Asia.* Pancake tortoise: from Tanzania, named for its flat, flexible shell.* Starry night harlequin toad: found only in the mountains of Colombia.* Attenborough's long-beaked echidna: an egg-laying mammal from New Guinea, named for naturalist David Attenborough, who is 100.A major goal of the programme is to provide sustained funding to conservation efforts that have often operated with limited resources despite showing promising results."This funding, this global platform and technical support change what is possible," Tiana Andriamanana, executive director of Association Fanamby, one of the organisations receiving support through the initiative, said in a statement.She noted that conservationists had worked for years to protect the golden-crowned sifaka despite limited budgets, adding that allowing the species to disappear "was never an option."The launch of the Phoenix Species Project comes as scientists are continuously warning about the accelerating loss of biodiversity around the world, as thousands of plans and animal species are witnessing increasing risks from human activity, habitat destruction and climate change. The organisers now hope that the fund created by Jeff Bezos and DiCaprio will help reverse declines and also create long-term recovery pathways for some of the most vulnerable wildlife of the planet.
Article Summary: The Phoenix Species Project is the largest fund dedicated exclusively to recovering critically endangered species. The initiative is being led by Re:wild, the conservation organisation co-founded by Dicaprio, and the Bezos Earth Fund, chaired by Bezos. The program is said to offer funding, technical expertise and long-term support to conservation groups.

Article Title: India’s startup boom masks a growing wellbeing crisis: Study
Article Text: Nearly half of those working in India's startup ecosystem reported low levels of mental wellbeing, with employees faring worse than founders and investors, according to a new study released ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10.The *State of Mind: The Startup Ecosystem* report found that 47.5% of respondents scored at or below its wellbeing threshold. Among startup employees, the figure rose to 54.3%, compared with 42.9% among founders, 45.2% among investors and 44.2% among other ecosystem stakeholders.The study, which surveyed 823 people across India, also found a strong link between mental wellbeing and psychological safety at work, or how comfortable people feel admitting that they are struggling.Overall, 34.8% of respondents said they felt unsafe speaking up. Among employees who felt this way, 88.3% scored low on wellbeing, compared with 26.7% of employees who felt safe acknowledging difficulties.Another finding was the gap between how people assessed their own mental health and what their wellbeing scores suggested. Of the 391 respondents who scored below the threshold, 35.3% still described themselves as thriving or doing okay.Only 15.1% reported seeking professional help.The study was initiated by Sheetal Bahl, Founder and Partner at venture capital firm Merak Ventures, and authored by Priyanka Kartari, Dr Sukhmani Pal and Dr Dilip Panniker.“To those who are part of it, it will unlikely come as a surprise how poorly the ecosystem is faring. But this study highlights some nuances, like while all groups show concerning results, it is employees who carry the largest share of stress,” Bahl said.“The silver lining is that the fixes are not rocket science – make it safer for people to speak up, give them some support, and allow them real time-off, and the wellbeing improves dramatically,” he added.The initiative is supported by study's co-authors and 1mg co-founder Gaurav Agarwal and Akshit Mathur.The report also draws attention to the business implications of poor mental health, citing industry findings that associate prolonged exhaustion with entrepreneurs leaving their businesses and employees taking more sick leave or looking for other jobs.It recommends regular anonymous wellbeing assessments, confidential support systems, training for managers and protected time off. Investors, too, have a role to play, the report suggests, by factoring wellbeing into due diligence and supporting mental health initiatives within their portfolio companies.The research used an adapted version of the World Health Organization's Five-item Well-Being Index, alongside respondents' own assessments of their wellbeing.Of the 1,040 survey submissions received, 823 were retained for analysis, including 347 founders or co-founders, 300 employees, 124 investors and 52 ecosystem supporters.The researchers cautioned that the survey was self-selected and captured responses at a single point in time. The wellbeing threshold used has not been independently validated for the adapted index, and the findings do not establish clinical diagnoses or a causal relationship between workplace conditions and mental health. The difference in wellbeing between founders and employees also narrowed after accounting for demographic factors and working hours.The report, released ahead of World Mental Health Day, calls for more sustained attention to mental health across India's startup ecosystem, particularly among employees whose difficulties may otherwise go unrecognised.
Article Summary: Nearly half of those working in India's startup ecosystem reported low levels of mental wellbeing. Employees faring worse than founders and investors, according to a new study released ahead of World Mental Health Day on October 10. Report calls for more sustained attention to mental health across the startup ecosystem.

Article Title: Google Cloud launches universal ‘Gemini Agent’ with deep app integration
Article Text:
How Google’s Gemini Agent operates

Unified Interface and API:

Omnipresent and headless deployment:

Multi-agent orchestration:

Deep integration across Google Workspace apps

Personal Assistance:

Google Cloud unveiled the Gemini agent at its annual Gemini at Work 2026 conference, positioning the system as a universal, single digital assistant engineered to handle enterprise knowledge work, run complex code and execute multi-step workflows straight from a prompt box. According to Google Cloud, nearly 500 enterprise customers each processed over one trillion tokens in the past year alone. Furthermore, approximately 80% of all Google Cloud clients now deploy its artificial intelligence offerings, while nearly 90% of Fortune 100 enterprises actively use Gemini Enterprise. With business environments pivoting toward agentic systems, Google stated that the new Gemini agent is built around delegating end objectives rather than micromanaging step-by-step instructions.The Gemini agent is designed around six core architectural pillars.Users can chat, delegate autonomous objectives, schedule background duties, and generate code from a consolidated interface without switching between disconnected applications.The system functions across web interfaces, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. It integrates directly into developer command lines, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack, or operates headlessly behind third-party enterprise tools.Running entirely on cloud infrastructure, the agent retains a shared memory bank and personalization graph across all endpoints. Users can initiate a job that runs for hours or days, close their computer, and return to completed deliverables without re-briefing the system.When handling complex projects, Gemini can spin up specialised, temporary sub-agents to tackle parallel or sequential tasks. It can also stand up permanent "coworker agents" assigned to specific team functions. These coworker agents receive their own dedicated email addresses (such as @agents.company.com), independent cloud storage, and role boundaries.The system retains four distinct layers of memory: session memory for active jobs; semantic memory for company documentation; procedural memory for repeatable workflows; and episodic memory to recall past interactions.Flexible multi-model routing: The agent decouples the user experience from the underlying foundation model. It dynamically routes queries to the most cost-effective and accurate engine available, navigating Google’s own Gemini family alongside Anthropic’s Claude models, with support for future private and open-source models.The agent works directly across Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides, Sheets, Chat and Calendar through three primary modes:Knowing a user’s schedule and team relationships, the agent can coordinate across apps automatically. For example, it can assemble an attendee list from past chat threads, review calendars, and send scheduling emails without requiring manual contact entry.Built-in Workspace Intelligence identifies tasks within inbound emails, such as a manager requesting a presentation, and serves up one-click prompts allowing users to delegate the task directly to Gemini. The inbox also highlights messages based on operational importance rather than arrival time.Departments can generate artificial colleagues that show up directly in corporate directories with their own calendar and Drive storage. Team members can tag the coworker agent in Chat or add them to document comments, where the agent suggests edits and answers questions under its own identity without exposing wider personal files.
Article Summary: The Gemini agent is designed around six core architectural pillars. Users can chat, delegate autonomous objectives, schedule background duties, and generate code from a consolidated interface. The system functions across web interfaces, iOS, Android, macOS, and Windows. It integrates directly into developer command lines, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Slack.

Article Text:
Shifting from wealth to 'Don't Die'

Anti-aging influencer and tech millionaire Bryan Johnson is urging the world’s richest man, Elon Musk , to reconsider their life priorities, offering pointed health advice to the tech mogul by stating that human survival should supersede financial gain. Appearing in an interview on The Axios Show, the 49-year-old entrepreneur, who reportedly spends upwards of $2 million each year in a quest to reverse biological aging, stated that society is approaching a turning point where wellness will outshine net worth.When asked what counsel he would share with Musk, Johnson expressed a desire to see the Tesla and SpaceX chief look after his physical wellbeing so he can reap the rewards of his labour:“I hope Elon would clean up his health. I mean, he’s worked so hard. He has a lot of potential to enjoy what he’s built,” Johnson said, as per Axios.Johnson also noted that he would welcome the opportunity to help President Donald Trump with his physical health, adding that world leaders frequently reach out to him for guidance and that he regularly participates in group chats with prominent tech executives and influencers.Johnson envisions a cultural transition away from traditional financial success toward his personal longevity mantra, dubbed “Don't Die”. His ultimate benchmark for success is whether future civilisations look back favorably on his pioneer work:“Will the 25th century … be like, 'thank you' in 500 years? Will they give me a head nod? That’s the goal,” Johnson remarked.“Society says making money … is the greatest trophy one can get … we are at this inflection moment as a species where we are transitioning to 'Don't Die.' What creates status and power and prestige is going to be different. And as crazy as it sounds, it may be your nighttime erections … It may be your ability to dunk a basketball at age 49. ”To guide his pursuit of biological youth, Johnson has turned his home into an advanced testing facility and gathered an enormous digital record of his bodily functions. Backed by wearables, a dedicated concierge medical squad and home diagnostic suites, Johnson is said to have amassed over 4.2 billion individual data points concerning his physiology, deploying AI software to detect trends and draw actionable conclusions.In 2023, Johnson famously swapped blood plasma with his teenage son. While the experiment benefited his elderly father, Johnson discontinued it for himself after tests indicated his biomarkers were already equivalent to an 18-year-old’s.Johnson openly documents intimate metrics with his 8 million social media followers, sharing updates on everything from sperm vitality to nocturnal erections.
Article Summary: Bryan Johnson is urging the world’s richest man, Elon Musk, to reconsider their life priorities. The 49-year-old tech millionaire believes that human survival should supersede financial gain. Johnson has turned his home into an advanced testing facility and gathered an enormous digital record of his bodily functions.

Article Title: Popular VC Paul Graham disagrees with Amazon ‘ban’ on Meta's Muse and Perplexity's Comet AI; says that blocking AI Agents will backfire
Article Text:
Amazon’s pushback against ‘outside’ AI

Renowned venture capitalist and Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham has criticised Amazon ’s aggressive crackdown on third-party AI shopping assistants, warning that shutting out these automated agents may open the door for a startup rival to challenge the e-commerce giant’s market dominance. In multiple posts shared on X (formerly Twitter), Graham argued that consumer habits are shifting toward agentic workflows, and attempting to lock external tools out of storefronts will inevitably backfire by fueling demand for more open competitors.“Amazon banning agents is the first opportunity I've seen since Amazon was founded for a startup to create an Amazon competitor. People will want agents to buy stuff for them. It will be one of the main use cases. And they won't want to use some Amazon-supplied agent to do it,” Graham said.He framed restrictive platform policies as an open invitation for disruption, adding: “Any business that bans agents represents an opportunity for a startup to create a competitor. If they need to ban agents, it must mean people want to use them, or there would be no point. And that in turn means there's demand for a competitor that allows them.Your usage restrictions are my opportunity.”Graham’s remarks follow a series of defensive moves by Amazon to shield its marketplace from outside AI scrapers and purchasing bots.In September, Amazon confirmed it cut off Meta’s new Muse personal AI agent from shopping on Amazon.com on behalf of users. The retail titan stated that it took the step after trying unsuccessfully to convince Meta to voluntarily leave the e-commerce site out of the experience.Further, Amazon claimed it never permitted the access, noting that Meta failed to give prior notification, that Muse browse sessions do not identify themselves and that the tool appears to capture and store customer credentials, creating potential privacy and security vulnerabilities.Prior to the ban on Meta’s Muse, Amazon was in a year-long effort to block third-party agents across the board. The company filed a lawsuit against AI search firm Perplexity over its Comet browser and moved to prevent shopping agents built by Google and OpenAI from crawling its marketplace.Amazon launched Alexa for Shopping in May, an AI agent that researches products and makes recommendations.
Article Summary: Y Combinator co-founder Paul Graham has criticised Amazon’s aggressive crackdown on third-party AI shopping assistants. Graham argued that shutting out these automated agents may open the door for a startup rival to challenge the e-commerce giant”s market dominance. He framed restrictive platform policies as an open invitation for disruption, adding: “Your usage restrictions are my opportunity”
